company_name: Barrick Mining Corporation (formerly Barrick Gold Corporation)
overview: Barrick Mining Corporation is one of the world's largest gold producers and a growing copper producer, operating eleven producing gold mines and three producing copper mines across North America, South America, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific, with a greenfield copper project in Pakistan. The company renamed itself from Barrick Gold Corporation to Barrick Mining Corporation in May 2025 (NYSE ticker changed from GOLD to B; TSX ticker remains ABX) to reflect its growing copper business and a strategy built around a small number of Tier One, long-life, low-cost assets. Barrick sells gold bullion on the spot market or to refineries, and gold/copper concentrate and copper cathode to smelters, traders and exchanges, with over half of its gold production generated in North America (Nevada Gold Mines joint venture with Newmont).

business_model.summary: Barrick is a commodity price-taker that generates free cash flow by mining and selling gold and copper at the lowest sustainable all-in sustaining cost (AISC) possible across a portfolio of Tier One assets. Profitability is driven almost entirely by spot gold and copper prices (gold averaged $3,432/oz and copper $4.51/lb in 2025, both records) relative to the company's cost of sales. Revenue is transactional/commodity-based (no long-term contracts or recurring subscription-like revenue), though multi-decade mine lives at flagship assets (Nevada Gold Mines, Pueblo Viejo, Kibali, Lumwana) give cash flows multi-year visibility subject to price volatility.

revenue_streams.name: Gold (Nevada Gold Mines - Carlin, Cortez, Turquoise Ridge, Phoenix)
revenue_streams.trend: stable to growing (Goldrush ramp-up, Fourmile optionality)

revenue_streams.name: Gold (Africa & Middle East - Loulo-Gounkoto, Kibali, North Mara, Bulyanhulu)
revenue_streams.trend: recovering (Loulo-Gounkoto restarted Dec 2025 after Mali dispute)

revenue_streams.name: Gold (South America & Asia Pacific - Veladero, Porgera)
Copper (Lumwana, Zaldivar, Jabal Sayid)
revenue_streams.trend: growing strongly (Lumwana Super Pit Expansion, Reko Diq build-out)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - gold sold into the spot/forward bullion market or to independent refineries; gold/copper concentrate sold to independent smelters/traders; copper cathode sold to third parties or on exchange (e.g., LME). No material customer concentration risk since gold and copper are fungible commodities.
business_model.geographic_mix: Production: >50% of gold from North America (Nevada); remainder from the Dominican Republic (Pueblo Viejo), Africa (Mali, Tanzania, DRC), South America (Argentina, Chile) and Asia-Pacific (Papua New Guinea). Copper from Zambia, Chile and Saudi Arabia, with a major greenfield project in Pakistan (Reko Diq). Revenue is predominantly USD-denominated (commodity sales) while costs are incurred in a basket of local currencies (CAD, AUD, Chilean peso, PNG kina, Zambian kwacha, Tanzanian shilling, Argentine peso, West African CFA franc, Pakistani rupee).

competitive_position.market_position: Among the top two or three gold producers globally by production and reserves (85 million ounces of proven and probable gold reserves at year-end 2025), and an emerging mid-tier copper producer with two Tier One copper assets/projects. Operates the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture with Newmont (61.5%/38.5%), the largest gold-producing complex in the world, which the two companies have just agreed to expand via the inclusion of Fourmile and Newmont's Mike/Fiberline properties (August 2026, $1.95bn cash top-up to Barrick).

moat_factors.description: Portfolio concentrated in five Tier One Gold Assets and two Tier One Copper Assets/Projects with long mine lives (20+ years for several), providing lower unit costs and reserve durability versus smaller peers.

moat_factors.factor: Nevada Gold Mines JV / district control
moat_factors.description: Operatorship (61.5%) of the world's largest gold-mining complex gives Barrick control over shared infrastructure (roasters, autoclaves) and a pipeline of satellite discoveries (Goldrush, Fourmile, Ren) feeding existing plants at low incremental capital intensity.
Three-year rolling average gold reserve replacement near 190% and gold-equivalent net replacement over 500%, reducing the risk of reserve depletion versus peers who must constantly acquire ounces.
Operations span five continents and two commodities (gold/copper), reducing single-asset or single-country concentration, though this cuts both ways given resource-nationalism exposure (see risks).

Decades-long operating relationships and infrastructure investment in Mali, Tanzania, DRC, PNG and the Dominican Republic create switching costs for governments, but also expose Barrick to renegotiation risk as seen in Mali.

weaknesses: No pricing power - pure price-taker on gold and copper spot/forward markets
High geographic concentration of African gold production in politically volatile jurisdictions (Mali, Tanzania, DRC) with a recent history of operational seizure/dispute
Single greenfield mega-project (Reko Diq) carries large capital commitment, multi-year construction risk and is now under an extended security/cost review
Leadership turnover (CEO, CFO, Lead Director all changed within the past 12-18 months) creates near-term execution and strategy continuity risk
Complex corporate structure in transition (planned North American IPO/NewCo, Nevada Gold Mines JV renegotiation) adds near-term uncertainty to consolidated reporting and capital allocation

growth_drivers: Fourmile (Nevada) - 100%-owned discovery characterized by Barrick as one of the most significant gold finds this century; inferred resources grew to 13Moz at 16.9 g/t in 2025 from 6.4Moz in 2024, with a September 2025 PEA outlining ~600-750koz/yr potential production at AISC of ~$650-750/oz; as of August 2026, Fourmile is being folded into the expanded Nevada Gold Mines JV alongside Newmont's Mike/Fiberline properties

Reko Diq copper-gold project (Pakistan, 50% Barrick) - one of the world's largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits (37+ year mine life); feasibility completed Q4 2024; original plan targeted first production in 2028, though a security/cost review launched Feb 2026 has extended timelines (review period extended to mid/late 2027) and flagged potential capex increases above the prior $8.83bn (100% basis) estimate
Lumwana Super Pit Expansion (Zambia) - major copper growth project with 2026 capex guided at $750-850 million, driving a step-change in copper production and reserve life

Pueblo Viejo plant expansion and mine life extension, plus new Naranjo tailings facility - extends one of Barrick's highest-quality, long-life gold assets and was moved into the North America region ahead of the planned NewCo structure
Goldrush ramp-up and Ren project at Cortez/Carlin (Nevada Gold Mines) - near-mine, high-return brownfield growth feeding existing processing infrastructure

Planned IPO of North American gold assets ("NewCo"/"North American Barrick" - NGM interests, Pueblo Viejo, formerly Fourmile) - Board authorized management in December 2025 to prepare an IPO expected to complete by late 2026, intended to unlock value and retain majority Barrick ownership; now intertwined with the August 2026 Newmont settlement

Portfolio high-grading via divestitures (Hemlo, Tongon, Donlin, Alturas sold in 2025 for combined proceeds >$2.1bn plus contingent consideration) - redeploying capital from non-core assets into Tier One growth projects and shareholder returns

New dividend policy (50% of attributable free cash flow payout, fixed base + performance top-up) and expanded buyback program ($1.5bn executed in 2025) amid record gold/copper prices and record free cash flow ($3.9bn in 2025)

business.description: History of material disputes in Mali (Loulo-Gounkoto operations suspended Jan-Dec 2025, employees detained, $253m settlement payment, temporary loss of operational control), Tanzania and the DRC; the 2023 Mali Mining Code materially raised royalty/tax rates (Loulo-Gounkoto royalty now ~18%) and similar code changes could recur or spread to other jurisdictions.

A security-driven review launched in 2026 has already extended the project timeline and flagged possible capex increases on an $8.83bn (100% basis) project; delays or cost overruns would weigh on Barrick's copper growth narrative.

Simultaneous execution of the planned North American gold asset IPO (NewCo), renegotiation/expansion of the Nevada Gold Mines JV with Newmont, and ongoing portfolio divestitures creates integration, governance and market-timing risk.

business.risk: Reserve depletion / production decline at legacy assets
business.description: 2025 gold production fell 17% year-over-year to 3.26Moz partly due to the Mali suspension and divestitures; 2026 guidance of 2.90-3.25Moz is below 2025 actuals excluding divestitures, underscoring reliance on growth projects to maintain output.

Long-tenured CEO Mark Bristow departed September 2025; new permanent CEO Mark Hill appointed February 2026; new CFO Helen Cai (March 2026); Lead Independent Director changed twice within the year (van Beurden stepped down November 2025, succeeded by Loreto Silva).

financial.description: Costs incurred in a basket of volatile currencies (Argentine peso, Zambian kwacha, Tanzanian shilling, CFA franc, Pakistani rupee, PNG kina) against USD-denominated revenue; Argentine peso weakened materially in 2025 (ARS 1,031-1,492/USD range).

A $100/oz move in gold affects attributable EBITDA by ~$300m; a $0.25/lb move in copper affects attributable EBITDA by ~$110m; 2026 cost guidance is built on a $4,500/oz gold and $5.50/lb copper price assumption, both above spot-at-filing averages, meaning margin compression if prices retreat.

2026 guidance calls for total attributable capex of $4.0-4.45bn (vs. $3.0bn actual in 2025), driven by Lumwana ($750-850m) and Reko Diq ($600-700m, Barrick's 50% share), increasing near-term free cash flow sensitivity to execution and commodity prices.

regulatory.description: Mali's 2023 Mining Code precedent (higher royalties/taxes, state participation demands) could be replicated by other resource-nationalist host governments (DRC, Tanzania, Zambia, PNG).

February 2026 renewal of the Loulo operating license for only a 10-year term, with the application of the 2023 mining code still unclear, illustrates ongoing permitting uncertainty even after settlements.

The expanded Nevada Gold Mines JV (nearly 100Moz gold asset) required bilateral negotiation and a $1.95bn settlement with Newmont; any future IPO of NewCo requires Newmont consent and regulatory approvals.

macro.description: Gold hit an all-time high of $4,550/oz during 2025/2026 on central-bank buying, rate cuts and a weak dollar; analyst forecasts for 2026-2027 have been cut materially (e.g., Goldman trimmed its end-2026 forecast to $4,650 from $4,900; Kitco's survey median fell to ~$4,509 from ~$4,916), and a reversal in rate-cut expectations, dollar strength, or reduced central-bank buying would pressure margins given Barrick's 2026 guidance is built on a $4,500/oz assumption.

Barrick holds mostly fixed-rate debt, so direct interest expense impact is limited; however, interest income on its $6.7bn cash balance and gold's inverse relationship with real rates create indirect sensitivity.
2026 guidance flags higher costs for key consumables (e.g., sulfuric acid) and increased tariffs affecting cost of sales; oil price (WTI) and electricity costs are also meaningful inputs.
Copper prices are heavily influenced by Chinese physical demand; a Chinese slowdown would pressure realized copper prices just as Barrick ramps up copper capex (Lumwana, Reko Diq).

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold entered a historic bull market in 2025-2026 (average $3,432/oz in 2025, record high $4,550/oz) driven by central-bank buying (reported ~90 tonnes/month vs. ~17 tonnes pre-2022), rate cuts, a weaker US dollar and geopolitical uncertainty; forecasts for 2026-2027 have since been revised down from their peaks but remain well above pre-2025 levels. Copper benefits from electrification/energy-transition demand but is more cyclically tied to Chinese industrial activity; copper hit an all-time high of $5.88/lb in 2025.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate to high - gold is partly counter-cyclical (safe-haven demand rises in uncertainty) while copper is pro-cyclical (industrial demand); Barrick's blended exposure provides some natural hedge, but capital-intensive mine construction (Reko Diq, Lumwana) is highly sensitive to the commodity price cycle at the time capital is deployed.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct balance-sheet sensitivity (mostly fixed-rate debt, <$0.05bn variable-rate debt at YE2025) but high indirect sensitivity via gold's inverse correlation to real interest rates and the US dollar.

recent_developments.event: Shareholders approved renaming Barrick Gold Corporation to Barrick Mining Corporation; NYSE ticker changed from GOLD to B (TSX ticker ABX unchanged), reflecting the growing copper business.

Loulo-Gounkoto mining convention dispute with the Government of Mali: operations suspended January 2025 amid gold shipment restrictions; mine placed under temporary external administration June 2025; dispute resolved via a November 24, 2025 agreement (Barrick withdrew ICSID arbitration, paid a $253m settlement, Mali dropped charges and released detained employees); operational control returned to Barrick December 16, 2025; Mali renewed the Loulo operating license for 10 years in February 2026, though application of the 2023 Mining Code remains unclear.

Mark Bristow stepped down as President & CEO after nearly seven years (since the 2019 Randgold merger); Mark Hill (previously regional president, LATAM & Asia Pacific) named Group COO and Interim President & CEO effective September 29, 2025.

Updated Fourmile (Nevada) technical studies/PEA confirmed it as one of the most significant gold discoveries this century, with a preliminary economic assessment outlining ~600-750koz/yr production potential and AISC of ~$650-750/oz; inferred resources grew to 13Moz at 16.9 g/t.

Portfolio optimization: completed sales of the Hemlo gold mine (Canada, up to $1.09bn), the Tongon gold mine (Cote d'Ivoire, up to $305m), the 50% interest in the Donlin Gold project (Alaska, $1bn) and the Alturas project (Chile, $50m plus royalty) for combined cash proceeds exceeding $2.1bn in 2025.

Board authorized management to prepare an IPO of a new entity ("NewCo"/"North American Barrick") holding Barrick's Nevada Gold Mines JV interest, Pueblo Viejo and (originally) the wholly-owned Fourmile project, with Barrick retaining majority ownership; IPO targeted for completion by late 2026.
Helen Cai (Barrick board member since 2021, ex-Goldman Sachs/CICC) appointed CFO effective March 1, 2026, succeeding Graham Shuttleworth.

Mark Hill formally appointed permanent President & CEO (ending the Board's search); new $0.42/share Q4 2025 dividend declared (+140% QoQ) alongside a new dividend policy targeting 50% of attributable free cash flow payout (fixed $0.175/share base quarterly dividend plus a year-end performance top-up).

Reko Diq (Pakistan) project review launched amid security concerns, subsequently extended; management flagged slower development pace and potential capex increases above the prior $8.83bn (100% basis) estimate, while reaffirming Phase 1 remains approved.

Barrick and Newmont settled all Nevada Gold Mines JV disputes: Fourmile (Barrick) and the Mike/Fiberline properties (Newmont) are being contributed into the expanded NGM joint venture (ownership unchanged at 61.5% Barrick / 38.5% Newmont); Newmont to pay Barrick a $1.95bn cash top-up, which CEO Mark Hill indicated would largely be returned to shareholders; the deal clears a key obstacle to the planned North American IPO.

Record annual results: revenue $17.0bn (+31% YoY), net earnings $5.0bn, adjusted net earnings $4.1bn (highest since 2011), adjusted EPS $2.42, operating cash flow $7.7bn and free cash flow $3.9bn, all records, driven by all-time-high realized gold ($3,501/oz) and copper ($4.72/lb) prices; year-end cash balance $6.7bn (all-time high); net cash position (net debt negative $2.0bn).

guidance.management_commentary: Management attributed record 2025 results to all-time-high realized gold and copper prices and highlighted the resolution of the Mali dispute, portfolio high-grading (Hemlo/Tongon/Donlin/Alturas divestitures), and Fourmile's emergence as a globally significant discovery. For 2026, management guided to higher attributable capex (Lumwana, Reko Diq) and higher AISC on both metals, reflecting conservative (above-spot-at-the-time) price assumptions of $4,500/oz gold and $5.50/lb copper baked into cost guidance, alongside inflation in consumables and tariffs. New CEO Mark Hill (appointed permanently February 2026) is proceeding with the planned North American IPO (NewCo) and, following the August 2026 Newmont settlement, indicated Barrick intends to return the majority of the $1.95bn Newmont cash payment to shareholders.

bull_case: Record free cash flow ($3.9bn in 2025) and a fortress balance sheet (net cash position, $6.7bn cash) support an expanding capital return program (new 50%-of-FCF dividend policy plus ongoing buybacks) even as major growth capex ramps up

Multiple embedded, largely de-risked growth options - Fourmile (world-class discovery now backstopped by an expanded Newmont JV and a $1.95bn cash settlement), Lumwana Super Pit, Pueblo Viejo expansion, Reko Diq - offer a multi-year production growth runway through 2028 and beyond without needing M&A

Resolution of the Mali dispute (control restored, 10-year license renewal) removes a major near-term overhang and demonstrates the company's ability to work through resource-nationalism episodes while retaining its assets

Planned North American gold-asset IPO (NewCo) could unlock a valuation re-rating by separating premier, lower-risk Tier One North American/Caribbean assets (NGM, Pueblo Viejo) from the higher political-risk African/South American portfolio

Macro tailwind from a historic gold bull market (record prices, sustained central-bank buying) and a growing, higher-margin copper business positioned to benefit from electrification/energy-transition demand
bear_case: Heavy reliance on politically volatile jurisdictions (Mali, Tanzania, DRC, Pakistan, PNG, Argentina) creates recurring resource-nationalism risk - the Mali episode (suspended operations, detained employees, $253m settlement, unclear mining-code application even after the license renewal) could recur elsewhere

2026 cost guidance (AISC up sharply for both gold and copper) and a near 50% increase in capex guidance to $4.0-4.45bn show rising capital and operating intensity just as commodity price forecasts for 2026-2027 have been cut by several banks, squeezing the margin cushion if gold/copper prices retreat from record highs

Reko Diq's project review (security concerns, extended timeline to mid/late 2027, flagged cost overruns above the $8.83bn 100%-basis estimate) introduces execution risk on Barrick's single largest copper growth project

Unusually high management/governance turnover in the past 12-18 months (CEO, CFO, two changes of Lead Independent Director) during a period of major corporate restructuring (NewCo IPO, NGM JV renegotiation, multiple divestitures) raises execution and continuity risk

Complex, in-progress corporate restructuring (potential NewCo IPO, expanded Nevada Gold Mines JV with Newmont) creates near-term uncertainty for investors around future consolidated financials, minority stakes and capital allocation priorities
